record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the computational complexity of the minimum bisection problem on weighted planar graphs, where a bisection is a bipartition whose two vertex classes have sizes as equal as possible?

evidence.quote: If ||Vi|−|Vj || ≤ 1 for any pair i, j ∈ {1, 2, ··· , k}, then we say that the partition is balanced. Balanced bipartition is usually referred to as bisection.

It is known that, on weighted planar graphs, the maximum bipartition problem is polynomial time solvable[31], but the maximum bisection problem is NP-hard, while the complexity of the minimum bisection problem remains unknown (see [37]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E, w) be an edge-weighted planar graph with nonnegative edge weights w : E → ℝ≥0. A bisection of G is a partition of V into two disjoint sets V1, V2 with V = V1 ∪ V2 satisfying ||V1| − |V2|| ≤ 1. The weight (or cost) of a bisection is the sum of w(e) over all edges e ∈ E with one endpoint in V1 and the other in V2. The minimum bisection problem on weighted planar graphs asks, given such a G, to compute a bisection of minimum cost.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem: is it solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard?
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of minimum bisection on (weighted) planar graphs appears to remain open: it is not known whether the problem is in P or NP-hard. Recent work has focused on approximation, including a polynomial-time bicriteria approximation scheme for planar bisection, while exact polynomial-time algorithms exist only for restricted subclasses such as bounded-treewidth graphs and grid graphs without holes.

status_evidence.title: A Polynomial-time Bicriteria Approximation Scheme for Planar Bisection
status_evidence.snippet: The previously best known approximation for planar minimum bisection, even with unit node weights, was O(log n).
status_evidence.claim: Exact complexity of minimum bisection on planar graphs remains open; only approximation results are known.

status_evidence.title: Algorithms for Optimization Problems in Planar Graphs (Dagstuhl Report)
status_evidence.snippet: It is open whether finding a minimum bisection for a planar graph is in P or is NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of minimum bisection on planar graphs is explicitly listed as open.

status_evidence.title: On the Minimum Bisection Problem in Tree-Like and Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithms for minimum bisection are known for bounded tree-width graphs and grid graphs without holes.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time exact algorithms exist only for restricted planar subclasses.
